overview.description: Genomic DNA is the organism's core code. For E. coli, a simple boil-purification in a heat block extracts the 4.6 Mbp chromosome. But chromosomes are hard to get back into cells - which is why plasmids are the real workhorse of synbio.
objectives: match an extraction method to your genome type
perform a simple boil-prep for E. coli genomic DNA
understand why chromosomes are hard to reintroduce into cells

steps.intro: Genomic DNA is the organism's core code. For E. coli, a simple boil-purification in a heat block extracts the 4.6 Mbp chromosome. But chromosomes are hard to get back into cells - which is why plasmids are the real workhorse of synbio.

instructions.title: Pick a method for your genome
instructions.description: Choose an extraction protocol that matches your genome type (ssDNA, dsDNA, etc.).

instructions.title: Boil-prep E. coli
instructions.description: For a quick crude prep, pellet cells, resuspend, and heat in a heat block to release genomic DNA.

instructions.title: Plan downstream use
instructions.description: Decide what you'll do with the DNA before extracting - reintroducing whole chromosomes is rarely practical.

submission.description: Extract genomic DNA from your host and run a small aliquot on a gel (after the gel node) to confirm high-molecular-weight DNA.
